title: Chiefs’ Rashee Rice speaks on ‘reality check’ summer that included jail time
content:
JOSEPH, Mo. — Kansas City Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice described his tumultuous summer as a “reality check,” as he spoke with reporters Tuesday for the first time since last season.

Rice, 26, violated his probation in May by testing positive for a substance found in cannabis. After being arrested, he immediately served a previous 30-day jail sentence — one that resulted from pleading guilty to two third-degree felony charges related to a 2024 highway car racing incident in Dallas.

Rice was released from Dallas County Jail on June 16.

“A learning experience. A reality check,” Rice said Tuesday, when asked to reflect on his summer. “Don’t focus on the past; focus on what’s going on now.”

The timing of the jail sentence was costly. Rice missed the Chiefs’ organized team activities and mandatory minicamp, and he also wasn’t able to rehab then at the team facility after he had a clean-up procedure on his right knee in May.

Rice said he had to work to stay positive while incarcerated.

“It was tough. Mentally tough. They gave me ways to communicate with my teammates still, as well as my athletic trainer,” Rice said. “Besides the hard times in there, I kept my mind right watching shows and as much (comedian) Kevin Hart as I can to laugh. Then without that, just communicating with everybody on the outside.”

Rice, a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2023, is in the last year of his rookie contract. That makes this year critical as he hopes to secure a long-term pact with the Chiefs or elsewhere.

So far, Rice has proven unreliable off the field. He served a six-game suspension at the start of the 2025 season after the 2024 incident in Dallas; Rice was required to pay more than $115,000 in restitution to the victims.

He’s also been a part of other negative headlines. In February, Rice was accused of assault by the mother of his children in a Dallas County civil lawsuit. Rice was not criminally charged in the matter, though, and the NFL did not punish him, saying there was “insufficient evidence to support a finding that he violated the personal conduct policy.”

Rice was asked Tuesday what he wanted people to know about him now.

“I’m 100 percent locked in on what’s going on now with the team,” Rice said. “Ready to go out there and dominate, and I’ve got a good group of brotherhood behind me.”

Rice’s training camp hasn’t gone perfectly. He started practices appearing to favor his right knee, while not sure whether he could trust himself to fully accelerate following surgery.

That burst has looked better over the past week, though, as he’s returned to full team drills and has quickly become one of quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ favorite targets again.

Rice acknowledged Tuesday that a contract year will be a part of what pushes him this season.

“It’s motivating. Honestly, just being able to be back on the field with my brothers right now is motivating,” Rice said. “That’s in the future. I’m just focused on what’s going on right now, and that’s getting better for the team.”

Even with the away-from-football turmoil, Rice remains a popular teammate. Some Chiefs players wore “Free 4” T-shirts before he returned from his suspension last season. Rice described himself Tuesday as someone who looked to uplift teammates.

“I’m a positive guy. I’m a great person to feed off, as far as energy,” Rice said. “A smiling guy, mostly at all times. Unless it’s time for work, I’m serious.”

Rice said he remained hopeful about his own future as well.

“I’m doing good mentally,” he said. “I’ve got the right group of guys around me. Good agents, good coaches. Small circle — anybody else outside that’s not part of the football team — just keeping my head straight and also keeping me in a positive attitude.”
